summary: François Jacob earned doctoral degrees at the University of Paris (~1938–1947, ~1950–1954). He held posts at the Pasteur Institute (1960), Collège de France (1964), the Cabanel Center, and was elected to the Académie Française in 1996.

Françoise Pommaret is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at INALCO and the University of Paris. Her career includes lecturing at INALCO and positions at the CNRS (~1993, 2002) and the Royal University of Bhutan (~2005).

Tibetologist Françoise Robin studied at INALCO and completed her doctorate under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). She served as director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership roles at INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).
Fred Pfeil earned degrees from Amherst College and Stanford University. He taught at Stanford, Stephens College (~1975–1983), Oregon State University (~1983–1985), and Trinity College (~1985–2005).
Linguist and Indologist Fred Porta held posts at Stanford University as a professor (attested 2012) and as a lecturer in the Stanford Language Center and Department of Classics (attested 2026).

Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College, Oxford (~1929–1933) and with Mahasi Sayadaw (~1953), and founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling.

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1910), and founded several literary societies.
Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, where he served as a professor from around 1971 to 2021.

Frederick M. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held positions at the University of Iowa as professor (attested 2006–2008) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Indologist and Tibetologist Frederick William Thomas studied at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Librarian at the India Office Records (1898–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under J. S. Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht (1938–1945) and Leiden (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), Emory University (1989–1996), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Heidelberg University under Rudolf G. Wagner, Günther Debon, and Günther-Dietz Sontheimer (PhD attested 2002), and held a post there attested in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987) and Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004).

Scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology Friedrich Alexander Bischoff completed PhDs at the University of Paris, supervised by Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1964–1982) and the University of Hamburg (1982–1993).

Indologist and linguist Friedrich August Rosen studied at Leipzig and Berlin, the latter under Franz Bopp. He was a professor of oriental languages at University College London (1828–1831) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

Friedrich August Wolf, a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology, studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1777–1779). He held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1783 to 1807.

Friedrich Bechtel, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He worked as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) before becoming professor of comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg in 1895.

Friedrich Bollensen, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied theology and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen. He later held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1851) and as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus was a scholar who held professorships at the University of Jena (~1868–1871), the University of Basel (~1871–1872), the University of Marburg (~1872–1888), and Kiel University (~1888–1895).
